title: Planetary Sciences (EMSC 3022)
text:
Slides / Navigation
Summary of course material for week 5 of EMSC 3022 (Planetary Science), 2025 edition.
There are two sets of lecture materials in this section of the Planetary Science course. The first is a guide book to the terrestrial planets of the solar system. We’ll review this material, but it is mostly there for you to browse for later lectures in the course.
There are three mini-lectures on how we probe the interior structure of planets focussing on seismology and thermal evolution (including a brief overview of mantle convection). You can navigate to this material from the sidebar (on the left).
These are links directly to the slide-shows in case your browser doesn’t like the embedded presentations !
You can read all of this material from this website. See the information below for details on how to navigate the slides and find all the additional material.
There are lecture-slideshows in this document that you can also follow at your own pace. There are full sets of lecture slides and are 100% available online.
You can see the slides in full-screen by hitting the f key and use Esc to return to the window.

title: Lecture - Introduction to the Solid Planets of Our Solar System
text:
In this lecture, we take a tour around the solar system and reset our perspective on the Earth so that we can visit our own planet with fresh eyes.

title: Lecture - Evolution of the Solid Planets of Our Solar System - 1
text:
In this mini-lecture, we are going to look at what is inside the terrestrial planets of the solar system and start thinking about how we can probe their interiors. Even for the Earth, this is not an easy problem but that’s where we will start.
It is probably helpful if you already had a look through the Solar System Guidebook

title: Lecture - Evolution of the Solid Planets of Our Solar System - 3
text:
In this mini-lecture, we think about the escape of heat from a convecting planet and how this works as a mechanical heat engine. This is the driving force for geology on the Earth and leads to plate tectonics. On other planets we see different styles of surface deformation reflecting the interior dynamics.
It is probably helpful if you already had a look through the Solar System Guidebook and the previous sets of Lectures Slides - 1 and Lectures Slides - 2
